title: Derive End-to-End Latency from Robotics Trace Events
summary: Pair boundary events by request identity and compute exact end-to-end latency on one declared clock.

runtime.image_status: pending OCI build; baseline worker exists
runtime.budget_status: actual shared worker limits; verified before publication

physical_contract: Events use integer nanoseconds from one shared monotonic clock ID. Each request has one input and one output boundary. No clock correction, stage-duration summation, nearest-time pairing or robot actuation is performed.

public_case_families: out-of-order trace events with correct IDs
large clock origin and zero latency
hidden_case_families: different clocks and reverse time rejected
sorted results and preservation at scale

provenance.authoring_notes: RobotPerf motivates explicit workload boundaries and correlated timing. The strict two-event schema is an original bounded trace-analysis exercise, not a complete ROS trace parser or critical-path reconstruction.
